blocks.text: Image generation is the reverse of the Vision API covered in the previous topic, the model creates an entirely new image from a text description rather than analyzing an existing one, this topic covers the generation endpoint, writing effective prompts, size and quality settings, and editing an existing image.

This topic covers the basic generation request, writing effective prompts specifically for image generation, size and quality parameters, generating multiple variations at once, editing an existing image, and content policy considerations.
1. Image Generation as the Reverse Direction

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: Building on the Vision API, image generation covers the reverse direction

blocks.text: Where the Vision API, covered in the previous topic, has the model analyze and describe an existing image, image generation has the model create an entirely new image from a text description, genuinely the opposite direction of the same underlying multimodal capability.
2. The Basic Generation Request

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: A text prompt goes into the image generation endpoint, producing a generated image as output

blocks.text: A basic image generation request sends a text prompt describing the desired image, and receives back either a URL to the generated image or the image data directly, depending on the specific response format requested.

code.content:
response = client.images.generate(
    model="dall-e-3",
    prompt="A minimalist logo of a mountain at sunrise, flat design",
    size="1024x1024",
)
image_url = response.data[0].url

blocks.text: 3. Writing Effective Image Generation Prompts

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: A vague prompt is compared against a specific, detailed prompt

blocks.text: This connects directly to the specificity principle covered throughout this course, a vague prompt, "a nice logo," leaves enormous room for unpredictable interpretation, a specific prompt describing style, subject, color palette, and composition produces far more consistent, genuinely usable results.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Prompt Style","Result Predictability"],"rows":[["Vague","Highly variable, hard to predict"],["Specific, detailed","More consistent, closer to what was actually intended"]]}

blocks.text: 4. Size and Quality Parameters

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: size and quality parameters control the generated output

blocks.text: The size parameter controls the generated image dimensions, and a quality setting, where available, trades off generation cost against level of detail, choosing settings that actually match your use case, a small thumbnail versus a large, detailed print image, avoids paying for quality or size beyond what is genuinely needed.
5. Generating Multiple Variations

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: The n parameter generates multiple variations at once

blocks.text: This connects directly to the n parameter concept covered in the earlier Chat Completions topic, some image generation endpoints support requesting several variations of the same prompt in one call, useful for reviewing multiple candidate options before selecting the best one.
6. Editing an Existing Image

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: An existing image plus an edit instruction produces a modified image

blocks.text: Beyond generating an entirely new image, some endpoints support editing an existing image based on a text instruction, modifying a specific region while leaving the rest unchanged, a genuinely different capability than full generation, useful for iterative refinement of an already generated or provided image.
7. Content Policy Considerations

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: A content policy check may reject a request that violates policy

blocks.text: This connects directly to safety instructions and moderation, covered elsewhere in this course, image generation requests pass through a content policy check, a request for disallowed content gets rejected rather than fulfilled, this is a real, functioning safety layer worth designing your application around rather than working around.

blocks.title: This connects to moderation APIs, covered later in this module
blocks.content: Just as text generation has content policy boundaries, image generation carries its own, checking the specific provider documentation for what content categories are disallowed helps design an application that works within those boundaries from the start.

blocks.text: 8. A Worked Image Generation Example

A marketing team generating concept images for a campaign writes a detailed prompt specifying style, color palette, and composition, requests three variations at once using the n parameter, and reviews all three before selecting and further refining the strongest candidate through an edit request.
9. Practical Cost Considerations

Image generation carries its own cost structure, separate from text token costs covered in an earlier module, typically priced per image and scaling with size and quality settings, tracking this cost explicitly, exactly the discipline covered in the earlier Token Optimization topic applied here to images, matters for any application generating images at real volume.
Worked Example

A developer building a product mockup tool initially writes vague prompts, "a product image," producing wildly inconsistent results across different generations, making it hard to maintain a consistent visual style across a product line.

Rewriting prompts to specify a consistent style, lighting, and composition template, reused with only the specific product description varying, produces noticeably more consistent, professional looking results across the entire product line, demonstrating how prompt specificity matters for image generation exactly as it does for text.
Common Mistakes

items: Writing vague image prompts and being surprised by highly inconsistent results across generations
Requesting maximum size and quality regardless of whether the actual use case needs that level of detail
Not accounting for the separate, per-image cost structure when generating images at real volume
Assuming image generation has no content policy boundaries and being surprised when a request gets rejected

blocks.text: Practice

Write two versions of an image generation prompt for the same general concept, one vague and one specific and detailed, generate both, and compare how much more consistent and closer to your actual intent the specific version produces.
Key Takeaway

Image generation creates a new image from a text prompt, the reverse direction of the Vision API, benefiting from the same prompt specificity principles that apply to text generation, with size, quality, and variation count parameters controlling cost and output, all operating within a real content policy boundary worth designing your application around from the start.
